description.overview: Step 2 of the Smartshift Retrofit process involves locking in-scope objects, performing code merges, and completing remediation activities using analysis results from both source and target systems.
detailed_flow: After customer approves the scoping sheet and provides feedback for Customer_Review, Cust_TOC, and Customer_Review TABU cases, a working ToC in the source (ECC) system and a working Workbench TR in the target (S/4) system are requested.
In-scope objects are locked to the working TR in the target system. Any locking issues must be reported to the customer.
Simultaneously, a safe-to-import analysis is performed and the ToC is prepared in the source system. Once validated, the customer is requested to import it into the target system.
After import, the ToC is also locked to the working TR in the target.
Objects are categorized into SERVICE SCOPE and TOOL SCOPE based on their nature and whether tool results are required.
SERVICE SCOPE objects are manually retrofitted. TOOL SCOPE objects are handled based on tool results, and merge activities begin once tool results are available.
After retrofitting all in-scope objects, remediation begins using UC, EPC, HCC, and S4 (ATC) results.
Fixes are implemented based on the results, completing remediation before proceeding to Step 3.

activities.1. Request TRs: After customer approval of scoping and related documents, request working ToC in ECC and a Workbench TR in S/4HANA.
activities.2. Lock objects: Lock in-scope objects in the target system. Report any locking conflicts to the customer.
activities.3. Safe to import & ToC preparation: Perform safe-to-import analysis and prepare ToC in the ECC system.
activities.4. ToC import & locking: Once validated, have the customer import the ToC to the target system and lock it to the working TR.
activities.5. Object categorization: Split objects into SERVICE SCOPE (manual) and TOOL SCOPE (tool-driven).
activities.6. Retrofit execution: Start retrofitting SERVICE SCOPE objects. Begin TOOL SCOPE merging once tool results are received.
activities.7. Remediation analysis: Run UC, EPC, HCC, and ATC results to identify post-merge issues.
activities.8. Fix implementation: Analyze the results and apply required fixes as part of remediation.

comparison notes.context: This step ensures code consistency between ECC and S/4HANA systems while retaining target customizations. Proper classification and sequencing of object handling are crucial to successful retrofit and remediation.

common_errors: Locking conflicts on IN-scope objects in the target system
Delays in customer importing ToC to target system
best_practices: Ensure timely coordination with customer for TRs and ToC
Always validate ToC before requesting import
Clearly follow object categorization to avoid confusion
Begin SERVICE SCOPE retrofitting early while waiting for tool results
Run and analyze all remediation fixes thoroughly before closing the stage

chatbot_responses.what is step 2 in retrofit?: Step 2 is the actual 'Retrofit' stage where in-scope objects are locked, merged, and remediated based on tool and manual processes.
chatbot_responses.what are SERVICE and TOOL scope objects?: SERVICE SCOPE objects are manually retrofitted (e.g., TABL, DOMA, FORM), while TOOL SCOPE objects (e.g., PROG, FUNC, CLAS) require tool-based merge and analysis.
chatbot_responses.how is remediation done?: Remediation is performed by running UC, EPC, HCC, and S4 (ATC) tools and applying fixes to the merged code to ensure stability.
chatbot_responses.what happens if object locking fails?: Locking conflicts must be reported back to the customer immediately for resolution before proceeding.
